correctness.rationale: For every n and m, the nondecreasing legal parent list gives a reversible BFS-ordered plane tree. Independent-set sizes containing vertex i satisfy b_i=1+max_{j<=p_i}b_j=1+b_{p_i}, which equals tree depth. A constructive greedy partition yields alpha consecutive cliques, and any clique partition has at least alpha blocks. Standard formal-series plane-tree recursion proves the exact rational count. A standalone finite program independently checks all n<=9 graphs for alpha, clique partition and tree reconstruction and agrees with Dyck-height DP; the infinite conclusion is obtained by proof, not by finite extrapolation. Boundary conditions m>=1,n>=1, disconnected graphs and n=0 generating function convention are explicit.

evidence: Bacher, arXiv:1303.2724v1, Equation (1) gives rational bounded-excursion generating functions for general steps; it does not classify m-Abelian graph subclasses.

Saitoh et al. 2010 describe balanced-string enumeration and a family tree for unlabeled connected proper interval graphs; their tree is an enumeration parent-child hierarchy among graph representations, not the breadth-first tree on graph vertex labels with height equal to alpha.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Classical formulas for bounded-height Dyck excursions strongly cover the enumerative final step once an equinumerosity is known; those formulas are expressly excluded from the originality claim. Their broader path coverage does not imply the new graph-to-tree height bijection absent an identification of the graph property.

evidence: The source paper establishes two-clique equivalence and m=1 count, then introduces all m without counting them.
Bacher gives a stronger theorem for counting already specified height-bounded paths, not a reduction from graph alpha.
The graph generator of Saitoh et al. treats unlabelled connected isomorphism classes, not the fixed area-sequence model.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: m=1 case follows from [1] and is included only for consistency. The new bridge alpha=kappa=height is not a consequence of known path enumeration alone. The full counting result follows from the new bridge plus known path enumeration; this dependency is explicit. The user-defined primary finding does not solve the open peak/peak-nesting polynomial questions.

evidence: arXiv:2609.38084v1 p.6 defines graph via area sequences; p.15 Proposition 4.2 gives the m=1 enumeration; p.35 defines m-Abelian and asks broader refined questions.

The ordinary Dyck path directly encoded by an area sequence does not generally have height equal to graph independence number: the zero-area sequence yields an edgeless graph with independence n, while its ordinary Dyck path has height 1.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Potential rephrasing as clique-cover number alpha or as Dyck maximum height was checked. The new BFS tree is not the original area-sequence Dyck path, so a known Dyck height formula alone cannot establish the graph class equidistribution. The m=1 case is prior, not new.

evidence: arXiv:2609.38084v1 cites existing Dyck height counts and odd-index Fibonacci sequence in Corollary 3.15; they are pre-existing path values.

The full graph corpus in that paper explicitly gives only the m=1 numerical class size; no table assigning the Fibonacci numbers to all 2-Abelian unit interval graphs occurs in the inspected result sections.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The same numerical coefficients exist in path databases, but a sequence match does not show an exact database of m-Abelian graphs nor supply the graph-class-preserving bijection. No new identity for the classical path counts is claimed.

originality.rationale: The new content is a reversible area-sequence to BFS-ordered plane rooted tree construction preserving independent number and optimal consecutive clique count. The 2026 primary defines the general class but only enumerates its m=1 instance; existing Dyck height rational functions are given full attribution, not claimed original. Cross-formulation and graph-family searches produced no stronger covering implication. Risk: alternate literature may already describe this same statistic-preserving bijection.
residual_risks: Other authors may have proved the same BFS-tree statistic identification using a different Catalan correspondence or the synonym proper interval order.
Classical bounded-height path numbers and the m=1 graph count are already published and cannot independently support an originality claim.
No claim about peak or peak-nesting polynomials, connected subclasses, or unlabeled isomorphism counts.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper introduces all m-Abelian unit interval graphs and seeks refined enumerations. The result delivers an exact all-m canonical combinatorial classification and counting series, translating an intrinsic graph optimization invariant into tree height by a bijection different from the original Dyck representation. This distinguishes the graph problem from simply restating a classical path formula, explains the known m=1 case and gives natural complete Fibonacci and power-of-three enumerations at m=2,3. It is mathematically motivated even though refined peak-polynomials remain untreated.
